blocks.text: A kidney is a reddish brown, bean shaped organ. Each kidney, has an adrenal gland on its top. The kidney and its adrenal gland are surrounded by a fibrous renal capsule. Each kidney has a convex and a concave side. A depressed area on the concave side is the renal hilum (also called hilus). At this point, the renal artery enters the kidney and the renal vein and ureter leave.
book_errors: The kidney and its adrenal gland are surrounded by a fibrous renal capsule.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The fibrous renal capsule covers the kidney alone. The kidney and its adrenal gland are enclosed together in a layer of fat and an outer layer of connective tissue (renal fascia); the adrenal gland has its own capsule.

Internally, a kidney consists of two portions. The outer portion is called renal cortex. It makes up about a third of the kidney's mass. The inner portion is called renal medulla. It makes two-thirds of the kidney. The renal pelvis is a funnel-shaped structure in the centre of kidney. Blood enters the kidney through a renal artery and leaves through a renal vein. The renal medulla consists of a number of cone-shaped renal pyramids. Urine is collected in the renal pelvis and exit the kidney through ureter.

blocks.alt: A kidney cut lengthwise. Under the thin renal capsule lies the renal cortex; inside it the renal medulla holds cone-shaped renal pyramids whose tips point to the renal pelvis. The renal artery and renal vein enter at the hilum and branch between the pyramids, and the ureter leaves the renal pelvis.
